title: Prospect Ask Summarizer and Quick Economic Approach
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success receive high-touch enterprise asks that vary widely in clarity and economic signal. Time-to-first-response and the PM team’s ability to produce a repeatable feasibility and econ band in under 3 business days is inconsistent. This creates long tails in the intake pipeline and uneven prioritization decisions.

Goal: Ship a lightweight operational artifact and a 3-step process that lets Sales/CS produce a canonical one-paragraph summary, a 1-row econ band (ARR impact / implementation order-of-magnitude), and a proposed technical impact checklist. The artifact will be created by Sales/CS using a short form, reviewed by Solutions Engineering (if required), and queued for PM triage.

Scope: Non-bug feature asks from enterprise prospects or customers. Focus on aggregation (grouping similar asks), producing an initial RICE-like score, and delivering an economic feasibility band suitable for sales conversations and PM backlog intake. Not in scope: detailed technical design, full PRDs, procurement/legal negotiations.
acceptance_criteria: A 1-page intake template (fillable by Sales/CS) exists and is discoverable from the Sales playbook
Process enables a PM to decide 'red/amber/green' go/no-go for more investigation within 72 hours
Template auto-populates a suggested econ band (ARR impact: <50k / 50k-250k / 250k-1M / >1M) based on three fields
Aggregated asks are grouped by problem-surface (e.g., routing/policies, private deployment, latency SLA) in the intake queue
At least one enterprise deal (pilot) is captured using the new flow as a canonical artifact during the pilot period
triage_rubric: Customer value: expected ARR delta or key metrics affected (explicit estimate or salesperson judgement)
Implementation fit: minimal changes vs. runtime/hardware constraints (banded: trivial / moderate / heavy)
Operational risk: affects SLOs, privacy, or introduces compliance scope
Strategic alignment: maps to existing product initiatives or creates new high-value capability
Time-to-value: possible ship timeline (<1 sprint / 1-2 sprints / multi-sprint)
example_workflow: Step 1 (Sales/CS): Fill the 10-field intake form and attach the customer email/conversation link (Confluence or Drive). Form auto-suggests econ band.
Step 2 (Solutions Eng): Quick feasibility checkbox pass (15–30m) and optional note. If 'requires engineering review', tag ENG and add to 'needs-technical-review' bucket.
Step 3 (PM): Within 72 hours, PM reviews, applies triage rubric, assigns priority, and either moves to 'Backlog' or requests a discovery spike.
Step 4 (Aggregation): Weekly script clusters similar asks and produces top-5 problem surfaces for the product council review

2025-02-18 — Ben Morales: Added econ-banding rules based on past 12 months of closed-won deal sizes; recommended thresholds adjusted.
2025-02-24 — Clara Wu (Solutions Eng): Reviewed feasibility checklist; flagged KV-cache & dedicated routing as frequent technical risk drivers.
2025-03-02 — Ben Morales: Prototype intake form uploaded to Drive and PR opened (see links). Scheduled pilot with AE team for 2025-03-10. Added script to aggregate asks weekly (lightweight Python).
notes: Tradeoffs considered: we keep econ bands coarse to avoid false precision; conservative bands encourage follow-up discovery. We deliberately do not push heavy engineering review into Step 1 to avoid blocking Sales. Future: if pilot shows >20% of asks marked 'requires engineering review', will add an SRE/Eng rotation for 2-hour review windows.
